name: Cable Incline Lat Pulldown
summary: A lat pulldown variation performed seated against an incline bench to stabilize the torso and optimize the line of pull for the latissimus dorsi.

setup: Position an adjustable bench set to a high incline (around 60 to 75 degrees) facing toward or away from a high cable pulley.
Attach a close-grip handle (such as a V-bar or neutral-grip handle) to the high pulley.
Sit on the bench with your torso firmly supported against the pad, reaching up to take a firm hold of the attachment.
Establish a stable foot position on the floor to brace your lower body.
steps: Initiate the movement by depressing your shoulder blades and driving your elbows down toward your hips.
Pull the handle down in a smooth arc until your elbows reach your sides and the handle approaches your upper chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom, focusing on a strong contraction through your lats.
Slowly reverse the motion under control, extending your arms and allowing your scapulae to upwardly rotate until you feel a full stretch at the top.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the handle down toward your chest, and inhale as you return the weight under control to the overhead stretch.
cues: Drive your elbows to your back pockets.
Keep your chest anchored to the pad.
Lead with your elbows, not your hands.

common_faults.fault: Lifting your torso off the bench to use momentum.
common_faults.correction: Keep your body pinned to the backrest throughout the entire set and reduce the load if necessary.

common_faults.fault: Pulling primarily through forearm and bicep flexion rather than driving the elbows down.
common_faults.correction: Think of your hands as mere hooks and focus on drawing your elbows down and back to engage the lats.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the eccentric short without achieving a full stretch at the top.
common_faults.correction: Allow your arms to fully extend overhead while maintaining continuous tension on the cable.

precautions: Ensure the bench is securely locked into its incline position and will not shift under load.
Maintain control of the cable throughout the full range of motion to avoid jarring the shoulders at top extension.
